summary: The candidate is correct with no mathematical gaps. The reflection orbits give the exact original census, and the reflected-intersection census correctly uses adjacent first-coordinate levels. Downward closure and nestedness justify the disjoint-pair estimate, including an empty ground set when n=1. The attained height is finite, concave, and upper semicontinuous; its relation to the exact number of nonempty integer levels holds also at integer terminal heights. The resulting lifted set and density satisfy every hypothesis of the accepted two-thirds density theorem in continuous dimension d+1. Projection of the selected lifted point yields the asserted reflected-density depth before halfspaces are chosen. The symmetric-pair argument proves the actual-depth bound for every containing ambient halfspace, including zero continuous normal, and the strict numerical comparison is valid. The zero-mass case and all closed-boundary cases are covered.
